title: hotfix: fix SLO enforcer regional backoff ordering causing thrashing
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Fixes a race in the SLO enforcer's regional backoff ordering that caused repeated regional failover thrashing under transient capacity pressure. Context: During last week's incident (SUP-4789) we observed the enforcer flip regions repeatedly when two concurrent backoff timers were scheduled out of order; this tripped the regional circuit-breaker state machine and then immediately retriggered failovers. This PR ensures deterministic ordering of backoff expiry and makes the enforcer idempotent for closely spaced backoff events. Changes include: reordering the backoff queue, making state transitions compare-and-swap based, and adding a short suppression window after a regional failover to avoid immediate retries. Testing and safety: unit tests for the queue, integration test that replays the incident trace, and a staged rollout (canary) with feature flag. Rollout plan: 1) deploy to canary region for 1 hour, 2) monitor SLO enforcer metrics and failover_count, 3) promote to remaining regions if stable. Related: ENG-2189, ENG-2191, incident SUP-4789. Release notes: "Hotfix: Prevent SLO enforcer regional thrashing under concurrent backoff timers."
